question: According to fans, what supporting cast context explains why Reggie Miller's playoff efficiency stat may be inflated compared to Jordan or LeBron?
ground_truth: Fans argue: Reggie played in an era with lower pace and usage, making 20ppg more impressive but less comparable. He faced one guaranteed All-Star guard slot taken by Jordan every year in the East. The Pacers built the offense around his off-ball movement — when defenses focused on him, teammates got open. This team context may have enabled higher efficiency than facing iso-heavy defensive schemes aimed at true ball-dominant #1 options.

question: What are the three main caveats Reddit fans raise against calling Reggie Miller the most efficient first option in playoff history?
ground_truth: 1) Low volume — he never topped 26 USG% and often went 6/8 FGA, so the sample is less demanding than true #1 options. 2) Screen-dependent — his game relied on off-ball screens, meaning teams could neutralize him by smothering him off-ball and forcing dribble creation. 3) rTS% rewards shooting efficiency but ignores playmaking, defense, and overall basketball impact.
